newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds continue to slip on Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds continue to slip on Monday.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities continued last week's tightening trend on Monday, with premium coupons leading the way, mortgage analysts said.
Quiet pervaded the market much of the day, disturbed only by the occasional up-in-coupon trade, according to traders.

Morning housing market data, which showed existing home sales fell to an annualized rate of 4.14 million units in July from a revised 4.16 million units in June, had little effect on Treasuries or mortgage-backeds, according to fixed-income analysts.
Late on Monday, 30-year discount pass-throughs had slipped 7/32 to 9/32 overall, while coupons of 8.5 percent or greater were off 2/32 to 5/32. Thin trading exaggerated the slide, traders said.
On Monday afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 6/32 at 100-19/32, yielding 117 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were off 7/32 at 100-13/32, and FHLMCs were off 7/32 at 100-20/32.
In Treasuries, the 30-year bond was off 16/32 and the 10-year note had fallen 11/32.

Weekly data on retail sales, as well as a report on August consumer confidence, could push mortgage-backeds around more than usual on Tuesday because many market players are on vacation, traders said.
Wall Street economists in a Reuters poll on Friday forecast consumer confidence fell to 104.4 in August from 107.2 in July.
